Q: The pod "Firebase/Firestore" required by the plugin "cloud_firestore" requires a higher minimum iOS deployment version A:

Error launching application on iPhone 15.

Step-by-step release solution required!:

Add to

./pubspec.yaml,

Under

environment:
sdk:

add the block :

minimum_os_version:
ios: '15.0'

Run in terminal

killall -9 Xcode

You have just closed Xcode

Do not open it for now.

Now run the entire following block of commands In the project folder

cd ./myApp

cd ios
pod deintegrate
rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/
rm -rf Pods Podfile.lock Runner.xcworkspace
rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/org.swift.swiftpm
rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/com.apple.dt.Xcode
pod install
cd ..
flutter clean
flutter pub get

Do not use flutter run!!

Open in Finder

project/ios

and look for the file

Runner.xcworkspace

Open it and it will open Xcode

When it is open and you are focused on it

In the top menu in Xcode (the Mac's up bar menu next to the battery icon)

Click Product -> Clean Build Folder

Then make sure you have selected the target

Any iOS Device (arm64)

In the top part of Xcode (next to the run button)

You will not be able to archive if you do not select this.

Click Product ->  Archive

Now he's putting the project on the archive.

When the archive is finished a window will open with your build file,

Close it,

Or delete old backups if you want.

After you close, go back to Xcode

Connect your iPhone with a cable to the computer

Select your

iPhone

as the target (next to the run button)

Usually if you see an iPhone model, it means a simulator

and not your iPhone. The iPhone will be listed as an iPhone

Then click the

run button

Now this is very critical!

Stay with the phone open in the run, the first run it will fail for sure, don't worry, it's because of lack of trust

Go to iPhone

settings -> General -> Device management and vpn

Trust your application

Then go back to Xcode on the computer

Click run again with the phone connected to the computer and the target on it

Now wait again with the iPhone open, when it's finished it will exit the application you're in and a white screen will appear,

Wait until the application loads

And that's it, you can disconnect the iPhone

Or stop the run on the computer

It will run for a week on the iPhone

Q: Pasting text into Android emulator clipboard using adb shell A:

There is an open source python script that can deal with the severe limitations: https://github.com/gcb/AdbPaste - and it works well enough except for long clipboard file uploads it's incredibly slow (200 line text file can take 20 minutes).

I found some code on GitHub for an app called clipper that can use adb to populate clipboard via a broadcast intent. I enhanced it to read from a file, the enhanced code is here: https://github.com/RoundSparrow/clipper

Build the app, install on the device. Now I can use ADB commands to populate the clipboard via a file. Works like a charm for a 3 page script I need to upload. Essentially you use like this:

adb push clipboard_content_file.txt /sdcard/clipboard_content_file.txt
adb shell am broadcast -a clipper.setfile -e filepath \'/sdcard/clipboard_content_file.txt\'

It's much faster AdbPaste, it takes only a second or two regardless of the size of the clipboard content.

Q: Comment portion of a line in a REG file? A:

I’ve run into this with .reg files too. As far as I understand, you generally can’t append an inline comment after a registry value the way you can in many programming languages. I usually keep comments on separate lines to avoid parsing issues. This registry file syntax reference is also useful when checking the supported format.

Q: How do I start building a custom AOSP-based OS for a POS device? A:

The OS will run only on dedicated POS hardware.

Do you know what chipset it has and the BSP support from the ODM? That would define long term longevity.

Users should not be able to install arbitrary applications from APK files, Google Play, or other sources.

This is possible to achieve in the framework / system apps layer.

I want to customize the boot process and possibly use a custom bootloader.

Every device has its own boot process, dependent on the chipset and ODM. What are you trying to achieve?

The device should boot directly into my POS application (kiosk mode).

It is possible to make a certain app the Home app and hide the system bars, etc.

System settings should be restricted so users cannot modify important configurations.

You could develop your own Settings app with limited options.

I may need remote updates for the OS and the POS application.

It is possible to implement the an Updater app which provides support for application and OS updates. You would also need to have a backend and deployment control based on certain policies.

I would like to remove unnecessary Android components to reduce the attack surface and improve performance.

This is a very broad requirement, but one could start somewhere like Secure Boot, etc., but all depend on the kind of hardware being exposed and then software specific hardening may be possible too. The fastest way is to be compliant with the ASB and vendor updates.

Q: How to create snippets like emmets in VS Code? A:

VS Code user snippets do not support Emmet-style multiplication syntax such as snippet*3 natively.

For example, this works in Emmet:

div*3

and expands to three <div> elements.

But a normal VS Code snippet such as:

{
  "My Snippet": {
    "prefix": "kvp",
    "body": [
      "key: $1",
      "value: $2"
    ]
  }
}

cannot be invoked as:

kvp*3

and automatically repeat itself three times.

If you need dynamic repetition (kvp*3, kvp*10, etc.), you need either:

  1. Emmet, if the syntax you're generating can be represented using Emmet.

  2. A VS Code extension that supports snippet repetition/templating.

  3. A custom VS Code extension/command that parses something like kvp*3 and generates the requested number of snippets.

So the short answer is: you cannot create true Emmet-style *N multiplication using a standard VS Code .code-snippets file alone.
